headline: Ukrainian and British Veterans Summit Nepal Peak on Prosthetics
meta_description: After losing legs defending Ukraine, Roman Havryliak and Christopher Greenwood climbed Mera Peak at 6,476 metres using prosthetics.
summary_short: Two veterans who lost legs in Ukraine's defence trained over a year to summit Nepal's Mera Peak on prosthetic limbs.
body:
Roman Havryliak and Christopher Greenwood each lost a leg while defending Ukraine. More than a year of dedicated training later, the two veterans achieved what many would consider impossible: they reached the 6,476-metre summit of Mera Peak in Nepal, climbing on prosthetic legs.

Their ascent represents far more than a mountaineering feat. It speaks to the resilience of soldiers who have returned home with life-altering injuries, and their determination to reclaim not just mobility, but adventure and purpose. The extensive preparation underscores the physical and mental demands they undertook to reach one of the Himalayas' high peaks.

Their climb stands as a powerful testament to human capability—a reminder that sacrifice in defence of one's country need not define the limits of what comes after.
quick_facts: Roman Havryliak and Christopher Greenwood both lost a leg defending Ukraine
Trained for more than a year before the climb
Summited Mera Peak in Nepal at 6,476 metres elevation
Used prosthetic limbs to reach the mountain's summit
